# Project description
Do dogs in different-income New York City neighborhoods have different names? We also want to compare those names with names given to babies in different decades. The wrangling involves preparing license records, combining annual baby-name files and relating postal ZIP codes to Census income areas. Area income describes a neighborhood, not an individual dog owner's income.

This draft runs dog–baby preparation and the proposed ZIP-to-income preparation in R, then attaches income and reports coverage without excluding dogs. The income preparation is a review proposal derived from Shweta’s contribution; its inclusion here does not imply shared acceptance. Income comparisons and the other three technical approaches are unfinished.

# Data sources
| Dataset | Organization | Format | What one source row represents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [NYC dog licenses, 2024 extract](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Health/NYC-Dog-Licensing-Dataset/nu7n-tubp) | NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene | CSV | One license record, which may be a renewal or another registration for a dog. |
| [National baby names, 1880–2019](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/babynames/limits.html) | Social Security Administration | Annual comma-separated text files | One name, sex and birth year, with its published birth count. |
| [ZIP-to-ZCTA crosswalk](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/GeoCareNavigator/ZIPCodetoZCTACrosswalk2024UDS.xlsx) | Health Resources and Services Administration | Excel workbook | One postal ZIP and its assigned Census area. |
| [ACS 2024 five-year household income](https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/groups/B19013.html) | U.S. Census Bureau | JSON | One Census area, with a median household income estimate and margin of error. |

## Attach income to the prepared dogs
Each dog has a recorded ZIP. The income preparation supplies one lookup row per ZIP, including its Census area, income estimate and status. A left join keeps every dog and adds the matching lookup fields. The dog’s name and baby-name measures do not participate in this join and remain unchanged.

The lookup uses `zipcode` as its key. Several ZIPs can share a ZCTA and its income, but each ZIP occurs once. No ZIP padding, geographic exclusions or income filtering happen here.
```{r}
#| label: attach-income-to-dogs
dogs_with_baby_name_measures |>
  left_join(zip_income, by = "zipcode") ->
  dogs_with_income

dogs_with_income |>
  select(source_row_id, name, zipcode, zcta, borough, in_nyc, income, income_status) |>
  preview()
```

## Describe which dogs have a geographic match
For this report, distinguish an unmatched ZIP from a ZIP outside the NYC selection rule. The lookup’s `in_nyc` value is TRUE or FALSE for every ZIP it contains. A missing value after this join therefore indicates that the dog’s ZIP was absent from the lookup.
```{r}
#| label: describe-dog-geographic-coverage
dogs_with_income |>
  mutate(geographic_coverage = case_when(
    is.na(in_nyc) ~ "ZIP absent from lookup",
    in_nyc ~ "Selected by NYC rule",
    .default = "Outside NYC rule"
  )) ->
  dogs_for_coverage_report
```

## Count geographic matches and income availability
Count dogs, not ZIPs or Census areas. Keep capped estimates separate from unavailable estimates: both have missing numeric income, but their status records different information. A missing `income_status` means no Census status was attached; it is different from a matched Census row explicitly marked “no estimate.” All categories remain in `dogs_with_income`.
```{r}
#| label: summarize-dog-income-coverage
dogs_for_coverage_report |>
  group_by(geographic_coverage, income_status) |>
  summarise(estimated_dogs = n()) |>
  ungroup() ->
  dog_income_coverage

dog_income_coverage
```

## Inspect examples from each coverage category
Show two source licenses per category so the summary can be connected back to actual records. This display does not remove rows from the prepared table. ZIPs remain as recorded on the earliest observed license selected for each estimated dog.
```{r}
#| label: inspect-dog-income-coverage
dogs_for_coverage_report |>
  arrange(source_row_id) |>
  group_by(geographic_coverage, income_status) |>
  slice_head(n = 2) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(source_row_id, name, zipcode, zcta, geographic_coverage, income, income_status)
```

DECISION: Review these categories before selecting the comparison population. No dogs have been excluded at this join. The treatment of capped estimates, missing estimates, unmatched ZIPs and the NYC selection remains for shared review.
